Applying this theorem to the present polyhedral Moebius band...”

This overstates or misapplies Schwartz’s theorem. The optimal paper Möbius band theorem applies to paper/developable/isometric Möbius bands of the relevant type, not merely to an arbitrary embedded polyhedral or piecewise-ruled Möbius band. Proposition 1 gives only that \(f(M)\) is an embedded non-self-intersecting polyhedral Möbius band, and Proposition 2 gives information about lengths of certain cross-segments/rulings and the boundary length. In fact, the construction uses affine squeeze maps that shrink the boundary edge and increase the other two edge lengths, so the resulting surface is not shown to be an isometric paper strip.

Thus the direct application of Schwartz’s theorem to \(f(M)\) is unjustified.

\[
S_1S_2S_3S_4\le C_2\sqrt{R_3R_4}\,V(R),

\[

\le C_2\sqrt{kS_3S_4}\cdot kS_1S_2^{1/2}S_3^{3/2}S_4

\[

\[

\]
The precise power of \(S_3\) is not load-bearing for Lemma 3.2: in either form, an uncancelled absolute length factor involving \(S_4^{-1/2}\) remains.

Because \(k\) and \(C_2\) are universal constants, a contradiction obtained by choosing \(k\) small must ultimately compare \(C_2k^\alpha\) to a scale-invariant quantity bounded below independently of the global size of \(S\). The displayed inequality does not do that: under simultaneous scaling \(S_i\mapsto \lambda S_i\), the right-hand side changes by a power of \(\lambda\). Obtaining such a ratio requires arranging the slice inequalities so that the absolute powers of the side lengths cancel. Hence the attempted extraction has the stated logical gap: one cannot get the necessary scale-invariant contradiction merely by substituting the two upper bounds into the \(34\)-slice inequality; one needs a matched use of the relevant slice estimates to cancel the leftover lengths.

\[
\sum_{r\ge 0} h_r(q|z)t^r=\frac{1+zt}{1-qt},
\]
so \(h_0=1\) and, for \(r\ge 1\),
\[
h_r(q|z)=q^r+zq^{r-1}=q^{r-1}(q+z),
\]
hence \(h_{r+c}=q^c h_r\) whenever \(r\ge 1\).

By the super Jacobi-Trudi formula,
\[
s_\mu(q|z)=\det\bigl(h_{\mu_i-i+j}(q|z)\bigr).
\]
If \(\mu\) is not a hook, then \(\mu_2\ge 2\). In the Jacobi-Trudi matrix, the first-row indices are \(\mu_1-1+j\) and the second-row indices are \(\mu_2-2+j\). Since \(\mu_2\ge 2\), all second-row indices are positive, and the first-row indices exceed the corresponding second-row indices by the constant \(\mu_1-\mu_2+1\). Therefore the first row is \(q^{\mu_1-\mu_2+1}\) times the second row, so the determinant is zero. Thus \(S^\mu(\mathbb C^{1|1})\), equivalently its super Schur character, evaluates to zero for every non-hook shape \(\mu\). Hook shapes are precisely the partitions satisfying \(\mu_2\le 1\), up to the usual harmless convention about the empty partition.
